nodes.label: Contributing guide

nodes.label: Security policy
nodes.rationale: Use private vulnerability reporting; public issues must not expose exploit details or sensitive data.

nodes.label: Mobile starter README

nodes.label: Mobile analyzer configuration
nodes.rationale: Activates Flutter lints and excludes build and Android generated code.

nodes.label: Flutter lint policy
nodes.rationale: Enables package:flutter_lints/flutter.yaml for Flutter analysis; generated/build Android paths are excluded.

nodes.label: Mobile package configuration
nodes.rationale: Declares Flutter dependencies and disables accidental pub.dev publication; description still says new Flutter project.

nodes.label: Recipient HTML entry
nodes.rationale: Loads the browser module and sets no-referrer and noindex/nofollow metadata.

nodes.label: API contracts
nodes.rationale: RPC ownership comes from the JWT; projections omit private fields and errors never expose raw AI output.

nodes.label: review_document RPC
nodes.rationale: Replaces reviewed medicines, records review time and invalidates existing shares.

nodes.label: search_prescriptions RPC
nodes.rationale: Owner-only reviewed matches use optional medicine and inclusive prescription-date bounds; reports undated count and limits results to 200 entries.

nodes.label: publish_summary RPC
nodes.rationale: Accepts only owner-reviewed medication IDs plus owner-entered allergy strings and notes.

nodes.label: create_share / accept_share / read_shared_summary / revoke_share
nodes.rationale: Creation stores token hash and fixed deadline; acceptance requires confirmed Google invited email; reads enforce bound recipient, expiry and revocation; only owner revokes.

nodes.label: Architecture
nodes.rationale: Separates owner-only originals and drafts, authorized medical snapshots and anonymous contacts.

nodes.label: Flutter Android owner app
nodes.rationale: Owner controls upload, review, publication, invitations and emergency contacts; physical-device walkthrough is pending.

nodes.label: Supabase Auth with Google PKCE
nodes.rationale: Account control is verified, not family relationships or professional credentials; live OAuth remains pending.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL with narrow RPC projections
nodes.rationale: Database derives ownership from auth.uid(); recipients cannot directly select private owner tables.

nodes.label: Private prescription image bucket
nodes.rationale: Owner-only access protects original JPEG/PNG files; client/service configuration must not expose a service-role key.

nodes.label: Authenticated prescription extraction function
nodes.rationale: An owned document ID selects one image for bounded draft extraction at ingestion; live image support is not yet verified.

nodes.label: Recipient browser
nodes.rationale: No application installation is needed; medical access needs the invited Google account and internet.

nodes.label: Anonymous contact projection function
nodes.rationale: A rate-limited token POST returns only intentionally public contact fields, never medical data.

nodes.label: Conservative source-change invalidation
nodes.rationale: Review or deletion clears all published medicines and revokes all medical shares, even for an unrelated source, to avoid stale source-backed snapshots.

nodes.label: Browser medical-display lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Visible browser polls every 15 seconds; local expiry, hidden tab, failed authorization or network check clears medical content.

nodes.label: Mobile session and record lifetimes
nodes.rationale: Records remain in memory; no encrypted local medical repository. Sessions/PKCE use secure storage, backups are disabled and FLAG_SECURE limits screenshots. Gallery originals and compromised devices remain outside control.

nodes.label: Event and prize research
nodes.rationale: Records official-source research dated 9 October 2026; host rules and actual live model use still govern eligibility.

nodes.label: Hacktoberfest Hack Day Barasat x CYCODERS Club
nodes.rationale: Research describes the Adamas University event; conflicting header/schedule end times need onsite confirmation.

nodes.label: Best Use of Gemma 4
nodes.rationale: Challenge eligibility requires an actual working Gemma extraction demonstration, not only adapter code.

nodes.label: Best Open-Source AI Project
nodes.rationale: A public licensed repository and reproducible meaningful AI use support eligibility; visibility alone does not establish approval or winning quality.

nodes.label: MLH open-source AI guidance
nodes.rationale: Meaningful AI use, public code, an open-source license and reproducible setup/model documentation are required.

nodes.label: MVP scope and acceptance
nodes.rationale: Bounds reviewed-prescription sharing and completion gates. Diagnosis, interaction advice, minors/guardians, offline/NFC, hospital integration and conversational RAG are deferred.

nodes.label: Owner-reviewed extraction draft
nodes.rationale: Gemma output is untrusted. Compare literal fields with the original, preserve unknowns and label manual entry; owner review is not clinical verification.

nodes.label: Bounded typed-prescription image scope
nodes.rationale: Accept one clear typed English JPEG/PNG page up to 5 MB; handwriting, PDF and DICOM support are deferred.

nodes.label: Reviewed medicine/date lookup
nodes.rationale: SQL reads reviewed records without AI, vectors or inferred equivalents; undated and conflicting dose records remain distinguishable.

nodes.label: Temporary selected medical snapshot
nodes.rationale: Invited Google account gets only selected medicines, owner-entered allergies and notes for exactly 24 hours from creation; every read checks expiry and revocation.

nodes.label: Public emergency contact QR
nodes.rationale: Anyone with the QR can see chosen names, relationships and phone numbers until rotation/revocation; internet is required and no medical profile is exposed.

nodes.label: Kin pitch pack
nodes.rationale: Use we are building until the live demo passes; no validated AI accuracy, clinical outcome or interoperability claims.

nodes.label: Prototype privacy notice
nodes.rationale: Fictional-only prototype; provider terms and retention governance need independent review before real patient use.

nodes.label: Inference-provider use boundaries
nodes.rationale: Provider receives the image. Google unpaid services prohibit sensitive uploads and medical-practice uses across tiers; DigitalOcean no-storage/training statements do not authorize clinical use.

nodes.label: Real patient use remains deferred
nodes.rationale: Server and inference provider process plaintext; no HIPAA, DPDP, medical-device approval or E2EE claim. Clinical/legal/operational review is required; research/data sales and trial matching are not implemented.

nodes.label: Retention and account-erasure design gap
nodes.rationale: Recipient copies cannot be recalled; operator logs/backups and account erasure need a separate deletion/retention design before public patient launch.

nodes.label: Fictional fixture policy
nodes.rationale: Every fixture must visibly say FICTIONAL / NOT FOR CLINICAL USE; fixtures are not model-accuracy evidence.

nodes.label: Visibly fictional software-test prescriptions
nodes.rationale: Fictional test records prevent real patient disclosures; the WhatsApp architecture image is not a prescription and is not committed.

nodes.label: Render deployment blueprint
nodes.rationale: Configures a static receiver with SPA rewriting and security headers; public hosting remains unverified.

nodes.label: Render static receiver configuration
nodes.rationale: Builds apps/recipient-web/dist, rewrites SPA routes and sets no-store, no-referrer, nosniff, CSP and Permissions-Policy; deployment is pending verification.

nodes.label: Agent contributor instructions

nodes.label: Synthetic-test evidence limits
nodes.rationale: Real local HTTP APIs and synthetic Google eligibility rows verify code boundaries, while browser display tests use mocked responses. Neither simulated identities nor local password login prove external OAuth, live image inference, clinical reliability or phone installation.

nodes.label: Web/backend, database and mobile checks
nodes.rationale: CI executes npm tests/backend checks/build, Supabase SQL authorization and HTTP integration tests, and Flutter formatting/analysis/tests. Real local APIs plus synthetic identity fixtures do not establish external OAuth or live inference.

nodes.label: Verification record · 9 October 2026
nodes.rationale: Records observed local/CI checks separately from external-service demonstration: Flutter 4, browser 7, Deno 5 and SQL 29 tests passed; backend check/build passed and npm audit had zero findings at implementation.

nodes.label: Passing CI authorization evidence
nodes.rationale: The cited CI run uses a real isolated local Supabase instance for ownership, forwarded-account rejection, expiry, revocation and publication limits; it is not an external Google OAuth login. Rejects unrelated linked Google emails and unverified provider emails.

nodes.label: Real local Supabase HTTP integration evidence
nodes.rationale: Passed in CI against real local APIs: private image upload/download, metadata return permissions, manual review, history, fixed snapshots, contacts and deletion. Uses synthetic Google rows and local password login; scripts refuse remote projects.

nodes.rationale: Neither Gemma provider was called with a live key; actual fictional-image request, model image support, real Google OAuth, public HTTPS receiver and physical two-account walkthrough remain unverified. No clinical accuracy or patient-safety claim.

nodes.label: Graphify evidence limits
nodes.rationale: Interactive Graphify map is a development aid, not a security audit; report records parser/deduplication limitations and unavailable exact semantic token counts.

nodes.label: Interactive Graphify architecture map
nodes.rationale: graphify-out contains interactive architecture data and an audit report; this development map does not establish security certification.

nodes.label: Threat model
nodes.rationale: Documents RLS, token, projection and device boundaries plus strict server-managed Google provider-email verification. Synthetic security tests do not establish real OAuth; prompt-injection, compromised-device/provider and operational risks remain.

nodes.label: Database RLS ownership boundary
nodes.rationale: Changing IDs cannot authorize cross-user records; backend gets owned rows and user JWT authorizes storage. Privileged service/admin keys stay server-side.

nodes.label: Random 256-bit tokens hashed with SHA-256
nodes.rationale: High-entropy tokens resist guessing. Medical forwarding still requires a Google identity that verifies the invited primary email and bound recipient ID; possession intentionally permits public contact reads.

nodes.label: Shared anonymous request rate limits
nodes.rationale: Database counters enforce per-token/global limits; a conservative global cap can deny legitimate use and no distributed WAF is present.

nodes.label: Strict Google provider-email verification
nodes.rationale: Server-managed auth.identities must contain a Google identity whose verified provider email matches the confirmed account primary email and invited share email. An unrelated linked Google email or unverified provider email is rejected; synthetic rows test this boundary and external OAuth remains untested.

nodes.label: Supabase Google provider implementation
nodes.rationale: The cited provider implementation supplies the Google email and its verification status used by the recipient eligibility check. A configured live OAuth callback and walkthrough are still required.
